 De'Andre Hunter 
 SAC 
 Forward-Guard 
 #15 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 De’Andre Hunter lit up the Pelicans with 24 points (7-of-13 FGs), five rebounds, one assist and four three-pointers on Thursday. 
 It was a rough start to the year for Hunter, but he was able to score a season-best 24 points in their previous game on Tuesday. In this one, he matched that mark, though he knocked down one less three-pointer. Hunter has been hot during this two-game stretch, but he won’t continue to score 24 points every night, and his lack of production in other categories makes him a difficult player to justify rostering. 
 De'Andre Hunter 
 SAC 
 Forward-Guard 
 #15 
 De’Andre Hunter finished Tuesday’s loss to the Spurs with 24 points (8-of-13 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), six rebounds, two assists, one steal, one block and five three-pointers. 
 Largely an afterthought in fantasy basketball despite being a starter, Hunter delivered one of his best performances in a while on Tuesday. Averaging 5.7 points per game in Sacramento’s first three contests, Hunter finished with his first 20-point game since December 22, 2025, as a member of the Cavaliers. With Keegan Murray (ankle) out for 10-14 days, Hunter should have more opportunities to contribute offensively. The question is whether he can do so consistently. 
 Ben Simmons 
 SAC 
 Guard-Forward 
 #25 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Ben Simmons suffered a ruptured Achilles tendon during Sunday’s practice. 
 Simmons’ 2026-27 season reportedly ended in devastating fashion days before his official return to the NBA. The 6-foot-10 guard/forward signed with the Kings with the expectation that he would back up rookie point guard Darius Acuff Jr. However, Simmons showed enough during the preseason to earn a starting spot alongside Acuff. Sunday’s injury changes that, obviously, with Precious Achiuwa and De’Andre Hunter being potential replacements in the starting five. As for the point guard rotation, Malik Monk will be asked to take on more playmaking responsibilities off the bench. 
 Keegan Murray 
 SAC 
 Forward 
 #13 
 Keegan Murray notched five points (2-of-3 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs) in Saturday’s exhibition against the Warriors. 
 With injuries limiting him to 23 games, Murray’s 2025-26 season was a lost one. He made his first appearance of the preseason on Saturday, logging eight minutes in the first quarter before being shut down. Murray’s return pushed De’Andre Hunter (four points, three rebounds and one assist) to the bench, and that’s likely to be the small-forward rotation once the regular season begins. As long as he’s healthy, Murray can be a valuable fantasy option. Another key for him beyond staying healthy is establishing a connection with rookie point guard Darius Acuff Jr. 
 De'Andre Hunter 
 SAC 
 Forward-Guard 
 #15 
 De’Andre Hunter (eye) accounted for three points (3-of-3 FTs) in Monday’s exhibition against the Lakers. 
 Hunter, whose 2025-26 season ended in February due to an eye injury that required surgery, was in the starting lineup on Monday. The Kings did not have Keegan Murray, so fantasy managers should not read too much into that. What they should read into when evaluating Hunter is that he did not have an official shot from the field, with his points coming via a three-shot foul. And there was no rebounding or defensive production to speak of. Hunter has rarely offered reliable fantasy value as a pro, making him challenging to trust in drafts. 
 De'Andre Hunter 
 SAC 
 Forward-Guard 
 #15 
 NBA insiders Chris Haynes and Marc Stein report that De’Andre Hunter (eye) underwent season-ending surgery. 
 While Hunter practiced on Wednesday, he has not appeared in a game since a February 6 loss to the Clippers. The wing, acquired from the Cavaliers at the trade deadline, was inadvertently struck in the left eye by Clippers wing Kobe Sanders, resulting in left eye iritis. Further evaluations revealed a detached retina, prompting Friday’s procedure. Hunter is the third Kings rotation player to be ruled out for the rest of the season, joining Zach LaVine and Domantas Sabonis. Hunter’s absence means more playing time for Nique Clifford and Daeqwon Plowden, with the former being a player who should be rostered for the rest of the season.

 #15 
 De’Andre Hunter (eye) is out for Saturday’s game against the Spurs. 
 Hunter will remain out for a fourth consecutive game as he continues to recover from left eye iritis. With Keegan Murray making his return on Thursday, Hunter’s absence led to Daeqwon Plowden playing ten minutes off the bench. There’s no need to stream Plowden while the Kings await Hunter’s return.

 De’Andre Hunter (eye) is out for Thursday’s game against the Magic. 
 While Hunter participated in Wednesday’s practice, he is not yet ready to play in games. The good news for the Kings is that Keegan Murray (ankle) will be available for the first time since late January. He should absorb a good percentage of the minutes that would go to Hunter.

 #15 
 De’Andre Hunter (eye) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice. 
 Injured during a February 6 loss to the Cavaliers, Hunter missed Sacramento’s final two games before the All-Star break. He came off the bench in that contest, with Daeqwon Plowden starting. However, Plowden did not remain in the starting lineup, and there’s no need to consider streaming him, especially with Keegan Murray (ankle) on track to return. 
 De'Andre Hunter 
 SAC 
 Forward-Guard 
 #12 
 De’Andre Hunter (eye) will be re-evaluated in 10 days. 
 Hunter has been diagnosed with iritis in his left eye after being inadvertently poked in the eye by Clippers wing Kobe Sanders during Friday’s loss to the Clippers. His absence opens up a spot in the starting lineup, with rookie Nique Clifford being the player most likely to fill the void. Given where the Kings are in the standings, Clifford and Devin Carter should have added fantasy value after the All-Star break.

 Darius Acuff Jr. finished Saturday’s loss to the Grizzlies with 38 points (12-of-25 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), five rebounds, five assists and nine three-pointers.
 After six games, it’s clear the Kings won’t impose any offensive limitations on Acuff. While efficiency can be an issue at times, that was not the case on Saturday. Acuff established new highs in points and three-pointers while shooting a respectable 48 percent from the field. He was especially good in the first half, scoring 21 points on 7-of-13 shooting and committing one turnover. The Kings play four games next week, starting with the Mavericks on Monday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Gregory Jackson

 #45 
 Player Stats

 GG Jackson recorded 21 points (7-of-10 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, two assists and five three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Kings.
 Jackson entered Saturday having made four of 13 three-point attempts over five games. Going 5-of-5 as he did against the Kings will give the three-point percentage a welcome boost, all the way up to 50 percent. Scoring in double figures for the third time in six games, Jackson also posted a season-high 21 points against the Kings. He still isn’t worth fully committing to in most fantasy leagues. However, GG may be worth considering in certain matchups, especially on nights when the Grizzlies are down a key scorer (Ty Jerome didn’t play on Saturday). 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Cam Spencer recorded 10 points (4-of-9 FGs), five rebounds, 13 assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Kings.
 The Grizzlies were without Ty Jerome (back) on Saturday, opening up a spot in the starting lineup for Spencer. In just 25 minutes, he matched his career-high in assists and committed no turnovers. When Jerome is available, Spencer is still worth a look in deeper leagues. He also needs to be streamed on nights when he gets the opportunity to start, especially for managers needing assists.

 Isaiah Stewart amassed 24 points (8-of-9 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), four rebounds and two three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Kings.
 Over six seasons with the Pistons, Stewart had nine games with 20 points or more. He recorded his first 20-point game as a Grizzly on Saturday, missing just one shot and knocking down two three-pointers. Beef Stew didn’t record any defensive stats against the Kings, but the offensive freedom he’s been granted in Memphis is something to watch moving forward. If he can produce consistently, that could make Stewart more appealing to some fantasy managers.

 Cameron Boozer accounted for 27 points (8-of-14 FGs, 8-of-8 FTs), nine rebounds, three assists, one block and three three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Kings.
 One game removed from recording his first career triple-double, Boozer scored a career-high 27 points on Saturday. While the season is still young, Boozer has been everything the Grizzlies hoped for when they drafted him fourth overall in June. The Grizzlies, who are now 6-0, play three games next week, starting with the Pelicans on Monday.

 Jonathan Kuminga accounted for 19 points (8-of-19 FGs, 1-of-1 FTs), six rebounds, three assists, one block and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Spurs.
 After attempting just six shots in Friday’s win over the Clippers, Kuminga got up 19 on Saturday. His percentage wasn’t great, but the shot volume should be there while the Timberwolves await Anthony Edwards’ return from knee surgery. The same goes for Jaden McDaniels, who finished Saturday’s defeat with 19 points, three rebounds, three assists, two steals and two three-pointers.

 Joan Beringer finished Saturday’s loss to the Spurs with 12 points (4-of-8 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), six rebounds, two assists and one steal.
 Beringer made his first start of the season on Saturday, as Rudy Gobert (back) was out. Unfortunately for the second-year center, he had to match up with countryman Victor Wembanyama. Beringer played 34 minutes, and his points and rebounds production were solid. If Gobert remains out for Monday’s matchup with the Bucks, that will likely be a more manageable assignment for Beringer.

 Ayo Dosunmu recorded 27 points (11-of-17 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), nine rebounds, three assists, three steals and two three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Spurs.
 Since moving into the Timberwolves’ starting lineup after Anthony Edwards’ knee injury, Dosunmu’s scoring output has increased with each game. His 27 points on Saturday were a season high, and he was highly efficient. Add in the rebounds and steals, and this was a good night for managers rostering Dosunmu. The Timberwolves play four games next week, starting with the Bucks on Monday.
